verifications.resolution: fednow_send: true (J.P. Morgan Payments commercial; not documented for Chase consumer/SMB channels). the participation baseline "unknown" should be updated from S915.

verifications.claim: International wire – USD capabilities: recurring = true, scheduled_future_dated = true
verifications.finding: DSA wire addendum allows repeating/future-dated transfers "except for Consumer International Funds Transfers"; for consumers, USD international wires are Consumer International Funds Transfers (30-minute cancel window applies). The chapter's own J08 MANAGE step says so.
verifications.resolution: Keep flags true for business; add other_flags {"consumer_recurring_or_future_dated": false} and note.

verifications.claim: International wire – foreign currency (FX wire / global transfer)
verifications.finding: The bank's terms name the service "Chase Global Transfer" (Online Wire Transfer and Chase Global Transfer Services addendum); sign-in entry is "sign-in-global-transfers".
verifications.resolution: Name: "Chase Global Transfer (international wire in foreign currency)".

verifications.claim: Most transparent SMB payables rail in the peer set
verifications.finding: Peer-comparative superlative cannot be verified from this chapter's sources alone.
verifications.resolution: Original stands as analyst judgement; FedNow portion corrected under JPM-C013. Synthesis team should confirm the peer superlative.

verifications.claim: Recipient has 9 succeeding business days to enroll, else cancelled (~10 days)
verifications.finding: Zelle Service Terms are internally inconsistent: section 11(d) says nine succeeding Business Days but later refers to a "ten (10) day period".
verifications.resolution: Original wording stands; it already reflects both numbers in the terms.

verifications.claim: Funds land in business checking usually within minutes; no incoming limit
verifications.finding: Business Zelle FAQ describes only a daily send limit; it does not state that incoming payments are unlimited.
verifications.resolution: "Usually within minutes; no incoming (receive) limit is published."

verifications.claim: former_names: ['PINACLE Express (lighter-weight operator tier referenced in PINACLE Mobile listing)']
verifications.finding: PINACLE Express is a current operator tier, not a former name: the PINACLE Mobile App Store description (v3.11.0, Oct 24 2026) offers the app to both PINACLE and PINACLE Express operators.
verifications.resolution: former_names: []; PINACLE Express noted as a current lighter operator tier in extra.

verifications.claim: former_names: 'PNC Popmoney (legacy P2P, pre-Zelle; not referenced on current site - INFERRED from industry history)'
verifications.finding: PNC's own 'Popmoney to Zelle' page still exists and states Popmoney was discontinued nationwide by its provider and removed from PNC Online Banking on June 24, 2023; its comparison table shows Zelle in the Mobile app only. The former name is CONFIRMED_BANK, not INFERRED, and the page explains why PNC has no web P2P.
verifications.resolution: PNC Popmoney (Online Banking P2P; discontinued and removed June 24, 2023) - CONFIRMED_BANK [S951].

verifications.claim: network_or_vendor: '... Visa/Mastercard (push-to-card, scheme unnamed) ...'; PNC-P14-S04 Direct to Debit Card network not named
verifications.finding: PNC's Oct 29 2025 press release names Visa Direct as the rail for its immediate push-to-card capability and says Direct to Debit Card is available via API and ePayments. There is no Mastercard Send reference; the ePayments schedule itself says 'Direct to Debit (Visa®)'.
verifications.resolution: Visa Direct is the push-to-card rail for Direct to Debit Card (API and ePayments).

verifications.claim: (absent) PNC-Visa Direct collaboration
verifications.finding: The chapter's recent changes omit the Oct 29 2025 PNC-Visa announcement, which expands immediate push-to-card disbursements (insurance, gig, EWA, refunds) for Treasury Management clients. It came eight days after FedNow.
verifications.resolution: Add 2025-10-29 PNC-Visa Direct collaboration to recent changes.

verifications.claim: PNC Mobile app ... 'new app experience' rolled out in phases from v5.4.0, 2025-2026
verifications.finding: On a re-read of the App Store Version History DOM (each note is paired with its version in the same list item), the phased-rollout sentence first appears on 5.0.0 (2026-05-15). The rollout ran in 2026 only, not 2025-2026.
verifications.resolution: PNC Mobile app ('new app experience' rolled out in phases May-Sep 2026, v5.0.0-v5.4.1; current v5.7.0).

verifications.claim: 2025-2026: PNC Mobile 'new app experience' released in phases from v5.4.0; v5.6.1 live Nov 2026
verifications.finding: The phased rollout started with v5.0.0 (May 15 2026). v5.6.1 shipped Oct 27 2026, and v5.7.0 is the current build (Nov 5 2026).
verifications.resolution: Single corrected line replaces recent_changes[1] and [5].

verifications.claim: Correction: phased rollout started with 5.0.0/5.1.0 (May 15-Jun 9, 2026), not 5.4.0; the 'released in phases' note disappeared at 5.6.0 (Oct 14, 2026); 5.7.0 shipped ~Nov 5, 2026
verifications.finding: The gap-fill table shifted release notes by one row. In the DOM the phased note is on 5.0.0 through 5.4.1 and missing from 5.5.0 (Sep 23 2026) onward. 5.1.0 is dated Jun 10, not Jun 9. The 5.7.0 date is right.
verifications.resolution: Phased note on v5.0.0-v5.4.1; dropped from v5.5.0 (Sep 23 2026).

verifications.claim: App 4.63 (Apr 2, 2026): push notifications for all available PNC alerts; app 4.61.1 (Dec 18, 2025): 24/7 debit card lock/unlock
verifications.finding: Same one-row shift. 'Push notifications for all available PNC alerts' is the 4.62 note (Feb 10 2026), and 4.63 (Apr 2 2026) is a generic UX release. '24/7 debit card lock/unlock' is the 4.61 note (Dec 4 2025), and 4.61.1 (Dec 18 2025) is generic.
verifications.resolution: App 4.62 (Feb 10, 2026): push notifications for all PNC alerts; App 4.61 (Dec 4, 2025): 24/7 debit card lock/unlock.

verifications.claim: The phased 'new app experience' (v5.4+) has drawn negative App Store reviews ...
verifications.finding: The new experience is v5.0+ (May 2026), not v5.4+.
verifications.resolution: '(v5.0+, rolled out May-Sep 2026)'.

verifications.claim: Scheduled and recurring Zelle payments exist (CONFIRMED_BANK, S017); editable until 11:59 PM ET the day before
verifications.finding: Only the Zelle Terms of Use (v2.7, Feb 2026, s.9) mention future-dated and recurring Zelle payments. The consumer Guide to Using Zelle and the Zelle page describe no schedule option, and PNC's Popmoney-to-Zelle page says Zelle does not offer future-dated or recurring payments. That page is undated and probably dates from 2023, but it is still live. Two bank sources disagree.
verifications.resolution: Keep the sub-product. Add an open question: 'Does the PNC Mobile app expose future-dated/recurring Zelle (Terms v2.7 s.9) given the popmoney-to-zelle page says it does not?' An authenticated app session or a current PNC FAQ would settle it.

verifications.claim: capabilities.scam_warning_interstitial: true
verifications.finding: No public PNC page, video or PDF shows an in-flow scam interstitial. The researcher's own open_questions say the wording 'requires an authenticated session'. Marketing copy ('only send money to people you know and trust') and terms are not an in-flow interstitial, so 'true' is not supported.
verifications.resolution: scam_warning_interstitial = 'unknown' (4 sub-products); other_flags.scam_education_content = true.

verifications.claim: RTP credit transfers capped at $1,000,000 (other_flags.cap_usd 1000000)
verifications.finding: PNC's RTP page does say 'Currently limited to $1,000,000', but The Clearing House raised the RTP network limit to $10M on Feb 9 2025. Either PNC still applies a $1M cap or the page is stale. The chapter presents $1M as the RTP cap without making that distinction.
verifications.resolution: Keep $1M as PNC-stated with a note: network limit $10M since Feb 9 2025; PNC page may be stale.

verifications.claim: Consumer-facing RTP 'Real-Time Bill Pay' ... a capability most peers do not expose to consumers [S018]
verifications.finding: The capability is in the DSA (RFP appears in the Mobile app; cannot be cancelled once authorized). The gap-fill site search found no consumer marketing anywhere on pnc.com, and no peer comparison was sourced. 'Consumer-facing' and 'most peers do not' are not evidenced. Biller reach is also unknown.
verifications.resolution: Reworded strength (see patch).

verifications.claim: Wire pages publish no cutoffs, status tracking, cancellation/recall path or fraud-reimbursement stance [S010, S004]
verifications.finding: The gap-fill wire agreement (S905) gives processing hours (business days 8:30 a.m.-6:00 p.m. ET), a cancel/amend policy (no absolute right; best effort) and a 30-minute cancel for consumer international transfers. Only 'no status tracking' and 'no fraud-reimbursement stance' still hold, and weakness[8] already covers them.
verifications.resolution: Reworded weakness (see patch).

verifications.claim: Zelle is mobile-app only; no web Zelle send documented
verifications.finding: Test challenge: absence of documentation does not prove absence. Checked whether PNC Online Banking offers Zelle anywhere.
verifications.resolution: Original claim stands.

verifications.claim: fednow_send: true (THIRD_PARTY)
verifications.finding: PNC's own Oct 21 2025 release never says 'send'; it only says PNC joined FedNow and expanded instant payments capabilities. The API catalog names RTP but not FedNow.
verifications.resolution: fednow_send: true (THIRD_PARTY) stands.

verifications.claim: (absent) UPIC, ACH Debit Block, ACH Debit Authorization
verifications.finding: PNC's small-business Cash Management page names money-movement controls and receivables products that the chapter leaves out: Universal Payment Identification Code (UPIC), ACH Debit Block, ACH Debit Authorization, plus ACH Debit/ACH Credit, Wire Transfer Services, Integrated Receivables and 'PNC Remote Deposit'. UPIC (a masked receiving-account identifier for ACH credits) and the ACH debit filters are material to an ACH-fraud comparison.
verifications.resolution: Two new sub-products (PNC-P14-S08 UPIC; PNC-P13-S10 ACH Debit Block / ACH Debit Authorization).

verifications.claim: (absent) FirstBank acquisition
verifications.finding: PNC closed its $4.1B acquisition of FirstBank (Colorado/Arizona) on Jan 5 2026. About 780,000 customers and 95 branches had moved to PNC platforms (Zelle, Bill Pay, PNC Mobile) by June 2026. That is a major 2026 change in the money-movement footprint and the user base for the new app experience.
verifications.resolution: Add 2026-01-05 FirstBank acquisition and the June 2026 conversion to recent changes.

verifications.claim: (absent) Congressional scrutiny of PNC Zelle scam reimbursement
verifications.finding: On July 1 2025, Sens. Warren and Blumenthal and Rep. Waters wrote to PNC's CEO asking for Zelle scam data and reimbursement policies, including for social-media-originated scams. This is context for the scam-reimbursement exception path. No PNC response was found.
verifications.resolution: Add as a context entry in recent changes.

verifications.claim: Bill pay UI is fragmented into three variants (Bill Pay Dashboard; two 'Pay Bills Summary' experiences)
verifications.finding: The Online Bill Pay page documents two instruction paths ('Virtual Wallet and Cash Flow Insight Accountholders' vs 'Other PNC Accountholders'). The 'Bill Pay Dashboard' is the scheduling screen used in those flows and in the consumer FAQ. Whether that adds up to three distinct live UIs or two paths plus a shared dashboard is unclear, and the help text may be legacy.
verifications.resolution: Add an open question. Only an authenticated view of both account types would settle whether there are two or three live bill pay UIs.

verifications.claim: Open questions list includes first-wave items duplicated by later, more precise entries
verifications.finding: open_questions[0] duplicates [3] (scam interstitial), [1] duplicates [8] (legacy Virtual Wallet automations) and [2] duplicates [9] (Bill Pay pay-a-person). The duplicates inflate the gap count shown to executives.
verifications.resolution: Resolve open_questions[0],[1],[2] as superseded.

verifications.claim: description: 'PNC is one of the seven Paze founding banks'
verifications.finding: PNC's Paze page says only that seven of the nation's largest banks, including PNC, currently support Paze. It never says 'founding'. The fact is broadly right (Paze launched in 2023 with seven EWS owner banks), but the cited bank source does not carry it.
verifications.resolution: Reworded description (see patch).

verifications.claim: TD Bank, N.A. total assets US$507B as of 2026-06-30
verifications.finding: US$507B is impossible under the US$434B OCC asset cap. TD's own Q4 FY2025 release gives combined U.S. Bank (TD Bank, N.A. + TD Bank USA, N.A.) assets of ~US$382B at Oct 31 2025 (US$388B on the consent-order measure at Sep 30 2025). American Banker (Aug 28 2025) reports US$386B, down US$48B since the cap.
verifications.resolution: total_assets_usd_billions 382 (combined U.S. Bank, Oct 31 2025; US$388B at Sep 30 2025 on the consent-order measure; cap US$434B)

verifications.claim: A TD Visa Debit Card is required for fast (within-minutes) Zelle delivery, else standard ACH 1-3 days
verifications.finding: The fee schedule lists the requirements for within-minutes delivery (Online Banking profile, U.S. address, unique mobile and email, ACH-enabled account, recipient enrolled) and does not mention a debit card. The Academy send demo (content/20, read live) gives the condition as both parties enrolled and the sender's instant limits not exceeded.
verifications.resolution: Within minutes when both parties are enrolled and the sender's instant limits are not exceeded; otherwise Next Day / Three Day ACH; account-number recipients 1-3 business days.

verifications.target: TD-J03/INITIATE/4 + exception 'Payer uses standalone Zelle app'
verifications.claim: Standalone Zelle app users cannot pay businesses
verifications.finding: The standalone Zelle app was shut down on April 1 2025. Its users had to re-enroll through their own bank's app, so the 'standalone app user' case no longer exists. The claim rests on S044, the older SMB FAQ PDF.
verifications.resolution: J03 INITIATE/4: payer uses Zelle inside their own bank's app or online banking (standalone Zelle app discontinued Apr 1 2025). The exception path is replaced by 'Payer's bank not a Zelle participant'.

verifications.claim: Help Center FAQ answer pages and TD Digital Academy demos are broken/unplayable, leaving no public step-by-step documentation
verifications.finding: Reviewer re-ran the Help Center knowledge base from td.com today: KB 2624, 2680, 2215, 3066 and 2315 return full answers. The Academy demos content/20 and content/171 load and expose every step. The gap-fill captured them (S901-S927), but the weakness still carries the first-wave wording.
verifications.resolution: Weakness replaced with the stale/contradictory-content wording in TD-C004.

verifications.claim: No published scam interstitial, in-app scam reporting, or scam-reimbursement policy beyond the generic line; three different phone numbers for Zelle issues
verifications.finding: Partly contradicted. A Security Reminder interstitial ('Only send to people you trust...') with a mandatory acknowledgment checkbox appears in the live Academy send demo, and the chapter lists it as a strength. The rest holds: no in-app scam reporting and no policy beyond 'Qualifying imposter scams may be eligible for reimbursement' (live business page). The three Zelle numbers are confirmed: 1-888-751-9000 on the business page, 1-800-493-7562 in the SMB FAQ PDF and 888-388-0406 in Academy content/153.
verifications.resolution: 'Only a static Security Reminder interstitial (mandatory checkbox); no in-app scam reporting; no published scam-reimbursement policy beyond "qualifying imposter scams may be eligible"; three different phone numbers for Zelle issues.'

verifications.claim: Consumer wires (domestic and international) are branch-only per third-party guides
verifications.finding: International consumer wires are in-person only. TD's own Foreign Exchange page and KB 2624 say so, so the evidence level can be CONFIRMED_BANK. For domestic, TD's live KB 2624 (re-queried today) says 'Currently TD Bank only offers domestic wire transfers in Online Banking', while KB 1398 says to visit a store. 'Branch-only' for domestic is therefore not established, and the evidence should not rest on third-party guides.
verifications.resolution: International: in person only (CONFIRMED_BANK). Domestic: TD's KB is contradictory (2624 vs 1398); status left in open questions pending a logged-in check.

verifications.claim: Verification method (trial deposits vs. instant) not disclosed publicly
verifications.finding: Disclosed publicly. Academy content/171 (read live) offers automatic verification with the external bank's online-banking username and password, or two small deposits. KB 3066 documents trial deposits under $10 within 2 business days. The product-level text and TD-J04 already say this, but the sub-product description and the open question were not updated.
verifications.resolution: TD-P02-S02 description updated; open question resolved.

verifications.claim: Zelle QR availability is contradicted on TD pages ('availability conflicting')
verifications.finding: The KB (3056-3060) and the Academy (161/162) confirm QR scan-to-pay and 'My Code' are live in the TD app, and the SMB Online Banking and Business Payment Suite pages market QR. The live zelle-for-business FAQ still says 'The Zelle® QR code feature is currently not available at TD Bank'. That is a stale line on the page, not an open question about the feature.
verifications.resolution: QR live (CONFIRMED_BANK); stale FAQ line noted as a content-quality issue; open question resolved.

verifications.finding: Read from the App Store version-history DOM (built-in browser): fund-availability estimates first appear in 26.3.2 (Jan 25 2026), not 26.3 or 26.4.4. 26.3 (Jan 14 2026) is the 24-months-of-transactions release. Spanish under 'Language preference' first appears in 26.4.5 (Feb 24 2026), not 26.5. SMB domestic wires with saved recipients first appear in 26.1.1 (Nov 5 2025); 25.12 (Oct 22 2025) carried the Bill Pay/Payment Center notes. Confirmed as correct: Disputes Center 26.7.3 (Jun 2 2026), SMB wire activity 26.6.1 (Apr 22 2026), Zelle limits 26.10.1 (Aug 5 2026), direct deposit 26.11.0 (Sep 16 2026).
verifications.resolution: Fund-availability estimates 26.3.2 (2026-01-25); Spanish 26.4.5 (2026-02-24); SMB domestic wires 26.1.1 (2025-11-05).

verifications.claim: (not mentioned) Bill Pay 'transition' releases Sep-Oct 2025
verifications.finding: App releases 25.11 (Sep 16 2025), 25.11.2 (Sep 28 2025) and 25.12 (Oct 22 2025) carry 'Updated features that allow seamless transitions while using Bill Pay' and a Payment Center redesign. The chapter lists the redesign but not the Bill Pay transition. It may signal a Bill Pay platform or vendor migration; no TD page confirms one, and tdbank.com/billpay shows no migration notice.
verifications.resolution: Add the recent change as quoted; add an open question on whether Bill Pay migrated platforms.

verifications.claim: Late or misapplied payment: Bill Pay guarantee not published
verifications.finding: Contradicted inside the chapter. The step's own friction field and the TD-J07 exception path cite the OBSA Bill Payment Service Guarantee (up to $50 in late charges if notified within 60 days of the Scheduled Payment Date). The action text was not updated, and the step cites S012 (fee schedule) rather than the OBSA.
verifications.resolution: J07 EXCEPTION/8 action reworded; sources S936, S012.

verifications.claim: External 'Instant Transfers' run over the ACCEL/Exchange debit network rather than RTP/FedNow
verifications.finding: The June 2026 terms define 'Payment Network' generically as 'a debit or credit network (such as the ACH Network or ACCEL / Exchange payment network)'. ACCEL/Exchange is an example in a definition, not a statement that Instant Transfers use it. The terms never mention RTP, FedNow or Visa Direct, and the chapter itself says live UI availability is unverified. Labelling this a differentiator overstates the evidence.
verifications.resolution: Remove the differentiator. Wording: terms define Instant Transfers over 'Payment Networks' (examples: ACH, ACCEL/Exchange); no RTP/FedNow/card reference; network and live availability unconfirmed (INFERRED).

verifications.claim: Business can send and request (limits $3,000/day, $15,000/month outbound)
verifications.finding: Incomplete, and the sources conflict. The June 2026 terms give Small Business 3-business-day outbound up to $3,000/day and $15,000/month, but within-minutes outbound up to $2,500/day and $10,000/month. TD's newer SMB Zelle FAQ PDF lists $2,500/$10,000 for both.
verifications.resolution: Within minutes $2,500/$10,000; 3-business-day $3,000/$15,000 per Jun 2026 terms (SMB FAQ PDF lists $2,500/$10,000 for both); inbound request $100,000.

verifications.claim: Commercial payables covered as Integrated Payables / ePayables / Embedded Banking
verifications.finding: TD's live payables page also lists Controlled Disbursement (plus full/partial account reconcilement and the TD Commercial Plus Card) as payables services. Controlled disbursement is a commercial check-disbursement money-movement service and is absent from the chapter.
verifications.resolution: Mention Controlled Disbursement and account reconcilement in the TD-P11 description (no new journey).

verifications.claim: Wires from ERP (expected Summer 2024)
verifications.finding: The live Embedded Banking page (©2026) still carries the footnote 'Availability of wires through ERP expected Summer 2024'. Whether ERP wires actually launched cannot be confirmed from public pages.
verifications.resolution: Keep the claim, annotated 'footnote unchanged since 2024; live status unconfirmed'. A TD Embedded Banking user guide or an RM statement would settle it. Open question added.

verifications.claim: Feb 2026: TD Bank Group 'More Human' brand platform emphasising digital-first
verifications.finding: No source is cited, and this is an enterprise brand campaign, not a U.S. money-movement change. The reviewer found no TD U.S. money-movement page that references it.
verifications.resolution: Remove from recent_changes_2025_2026.

verifications.claim: 2024 OCC consent order requiring supervisory approval for new products constrains the roadmap
verifications.finding: Not found in the OCC press release (S028), which mentions only a growth restriction. TD's own Q4 FY2025 release does state that the U.S. Bank is 'subject to OCC supervisory approval processes for any additions of new bank products' until the OCC accepts its AML program. The claim is right but should cite S031 as CONFIRMED_BANK.
verifications.resolution: Keep the wording; source list [S009, S031].

verifications.claim: Open questions still list items the gap-fill resolved (QR availability; external verification method)
verifications.finding: Both are resolved by S905/S912 and S906/S902 (see TD-C007 and TD-C008). The coverage self-assessment pages_blocked list also still includes Help Center and Academy URLs that now render.
verifications.resolution: Mark resolved: QR availability; external verification method.

verifications.claim: Customer learns wires are a store service; third-party guides state online wires are not available to personal customers
verifications.finding: The international in-person rule is CONFIRMED_BANK (Foreign Exchange page and KB 2624/2692), and the domestic online question is contradicted by TD's own KB. Neither should rest on Wise or GOBankingRates.
verifications.resolution: J10 DISCOVER/1 reworded; evidence CONFIRMED_BANK; sources S932, S902.

verifications.claim: Chapter's small-business product set (Zelle, Transfers, Bill Pay, Wires, Mobile deposit, ACH Service) is complete for SMB Online Banking money movement.
verifications.finding: The Small Business Online Banking page lists a 'MANAGE YOUR MONEY' tab set of Account Services | Mobile Banking | Bill Pay | Online Payroll | ACH Services | Wire Transfer | Zelle. 'Online Payroll' (Truist Online Payroll) is absent from the research dataset, research.md and the gap-fill capture. The product page says it pays employees by direct deposit or printed check, calculates and files taxes, is for 1-100 employees, and needs enrollment through Truist online business banking. Read in the browser and with WebFetch.
verifications.resolution: Add TFC-P09-S04 'Truist Online Payroll' (small_business; ACH_ORIGINATION; WEB): direct deposit at no extra cost or printed checks; automatic tax calculation and filing; employee access to pay records/W-2/1099; QuickBooks, AccountEdge, Zoho Books, Xero integrations; 1-100 employees; low monthly fee (more for >50 employees); enroll after registering for business online banking. Vendor not disclosed.

verifications.claim: Small-business Online Banking lacks documented in-product dual approval for ACH/wires (contact-validation codes instead); dual control confirmed only in Treasury Manager [S013][S045].
verifications.finding: This weakness contradicts the chapter's own strength and the TFC-J10 and TFC-J14 steps. The current Online & Mobile Banking for Business Service Agreement (eff. 9/17/2026, read in full in the browser with pdf.js) has a Dual Approval Feature in both the ACH Transfer Service and the Wire Transfer Service sections. It requires an 'Approver' or 'Approver Admin' and must be enabled by the Business Profile Owner. The 4/8/2026 agreement (S906) has the same clause.
verifications.resolution: Delete the weakness. No replacement is needed; the dual-approval strength stands (add 'Approver Admin' role and 'must be enabled by the Business Profile Owner').

verifications.claim: Public help content is thin: no bill-pay or mobile-deposit help pages, help-center index 404s; key journey details live only in PDF agreements [S005][S035].
verifications.finding: The gap-fill (S901-S905) found 18 mobile-deposit FAQs and 10 bill-pay FAQs through truist.com site search. In the browser I confirmed that the site search returns FAQ answers (for example q=international returns 6 FAQ answers, including the SWIFT/BIC FAQ). The finding still holds that there are no dedicated product pages (the /online-banking/bill-pay and /help-center URLs fail, per the blocked-pages list). A second, later weakness already says this more accurately.
verifications.resolution: Remove the first-wave line. Reword the later 'Public help content gap persists' weakness to: 'No dedicated Bill Pay, external-transfer or help-center landing pages (/online-banking/bill-pay and /help-center fail); FAQs are reachable only through truist.com site search (Zelle 39, mobile deposit 18, bill pay 10 results) and there is no external-transfer FAQ; key rules live in the service agreements.'

verifications.claim: Five first-wave app-version entries: 'App 4.0.0 (Feb 2025): Security Center checklist, external-account linking from home, recurring Zelle insights'; 'App 4.1.0 (Apr 2025): Truist Assist everywhere, add card to digital wallet (Paze), bill-pay payee groupings'; 'App 4.5.0 (Sep 2025) / 4.6.0 (Oct 2025): improved bill-payment confirmations...'; 'App 5.1/5.2 ... 5.4.0 ... 5.6.0 ...'.
verifications.finding: The App Store version history (WebFetch, plus the browser for 5.9.0) contradicts these entries. 4.1.0 (04/10/2025) is 'Bug fixes and Enhancements'. Assist everywhere, add-card-to-wallet and payee groupings are in 4.0.0 (02/26/2025). The Security Center checklist is in 3.4.0 (11/14/2024). Improved bill-payment confirmations are in 4.4.0 (08/14/2025). Account/routing payments are in 5.3.0. Mobile-deposit guidance and Siri are in 5.5.0. 5.6.0 is bug fixes. The chapter keeps both the wrong entries and the 'CORRECTION' entry, so it contradicts itself.
verifications.resolution: Remove the four first-wave app-version lines. Replace the CORRECTION line with: 'App releases (App Store): 3.2.0 Jul 26 2024 device widgets (Zelle, transfers, check deposit); 3.4.0 Nov 14 2024 Security Center checklist, external-account linking from home, recurring bill-pay/Zelle insights; 4.0.0 Feb 26 2025 Truist Assist everywhere, add card to device digital wallet, bill-pay payee groupings, Plan & Track; 4.4.0 Aug 14 2025 improved bill-payment activity/confirmations and external-account verification; 4.5.0 Sep 10 2025 payee-list cleanup; 4.6.0 Oct 27 2025 Assist search, 24-month deposit history, real-time external-account verification; 4.7.0 Dec 4 2025 security-settings navigation; 5.1.0 Feb 12 2026 multi-payee bill payments; 5.3.0 Apr 14 2026 new ways to pay using account and routing number; 5.4.0 May 7 2026 five saved User IDs; 5.5.0 Jun 25 2026 clearer mobile-deposit guidance, Siri balances; 5.9.0 Oct 28 2026 24-month credit-card history and streamlined check deposit [S919].'

verifications.claim: Paze positioning: 'Card Controls > select card > Digital Wallets > Paze > Get started/Activate; also 'Add card to digital wallet' (app 4.1.0)'.
verifications.finding: The Card Controls path is correct. The App Store note is 4.0.0 (not 4.1.0) and reads 'Add your credit or debit card to your digital wallet—no manual entry needed'. It does not mention Paze, and the wording describes push-provisioning to device wallets. Paze activation is a separate flow that redirects to the Paze site.
verifications.resolution: TFC-P07 positioning: 'Card Controls > select card > Digital Wallets > Paze > Get started/Activate (redirects to the Paze site to accept the Paze Service Agreement).'

verifications.claim: Home-screen Zelle widget (3.3.0); Transfers widget (3.3.0); check-deposit widget on home since 3.3.0.
verifications.finding: App Store: 3.3.0 (09/19/2024) is 'Bug fixes and enhancements'. The widgets came in 3.2.0 (07/26/2024).
verifications.resolution: Replace '(3.3.0)' / 'since 3.3.0' with '(3.2.0, Jul 2024)' in TFC-J01/DISCOVER/1 touchpoint, TFC-P02 and TFC-P05 positioning.

verifications.claim: 'or home-screen external-account linking (app 4.0.0)'.
verifications.finding: The 4.0.0 notes (02/26/2025) cover Assist, digital wallet, payee groupings, Plan & Track and rewards in Assist, with nothing on external-account linking. The gap-fill's verbatim App Store read (S919) puts 'Seamlessly manage and link your external accounts from the home screen' in 3.4.0 (11/14/2024). TFC-P02 positioning already says 3.4.0, so the journey contradicts its own product record.
verifications.resolution: TFC-J05/DISCOVER/1 action: "Transfer & Pay > 'Transfer money and pay Truist accounts' tile; or home-screen external-account linking (app 3.4.0, Nov 2024)".

verifications.claim: 'group payees (4.1.0)'; 'improved bill payment activity and confirmations (4.5.0)'; P03-S01 'payee groupings (app 4.1.0); payee list cleanup (4.6.0)'.
verifications.finding: App Store: payee groupings are in 4.0.0, improved bill-payment activity/confirmations in 4.4.0 (08/14/2025), and payee-list cleanup tools in 4.5.0 (09/10/2025).
verifications.resolution: J06/SET_UP/2 '(4.0.0)'; J06/EXECUTE_TRACK/5 '(4.4.0, Aug 2025)'; P03-S01 'payee groupings (app 4.0.0); payee list cleanup (4.5.0)'.

verifications.claim: Truist Assist 'accessible anywhere in app since 4.1.0'.
verifications.finding: App Store: 'Access Truist Assist ... from anywhere within the app' is a 4.0.0 (02/26/2025) note. 4.1.0 is bug fixes.
verifications.resolution: TFC-P08 positioning: '... accessible anywhere in app since 4.0.0 (Feb 2025)'.

verifications.claim: External transfer status: where 'Manage Transfers', states ['Scheduled','Pending','Completed'], evidence INFERRED.
verifications.finding: The current personal agreement (eff. 9/17/2026) states the status model directly: 'pending' until released, 'in process' until funds move, then 'complete'. 3-day transfers stay in process until the close of the third business day. The gap-fill quoted this from the 4/8 version but did not carry it into status_tracking.
verifications.resolution: TFC-J05 status_tracking: where_visible 'Log in to online/mobile banking (Manage Transfers)'; states ['Pending','In process','Complete'] ('Scheduled' for future-dated, inferred); evidence CONFIRMED_BANK; sources [S952, S907, S006].

verifications.claim: One View Connect: 'API-first embedded payments/reconciliation/reporting with in-ERP approvals ...; RTP initiation in-ERP'; rail RTP; dual_approval true. Strength: 'One View Connect embedded-ERP pilot with in-ERP RTP initiation'.
verifications.finding: The Oct 2025 IR release announced 'Real-Time Payments and approvals, directly within ERP platforms' as a pilot. The current public 'Truist One View Connect Features & Capabilities User Guide' (Rev. 04/26, 14 pp., read in the browser) only documents Information Reporting (balances, posted transactions, on-demand refresh and bank reconciliation in NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Dynamics 365 BC and Workday). It contains no payment initiation, RTP or approval content. The Treasury Resource Center page lists it under Platforms.
verifications.resolution: TFC-P10-S06 description: 'ERP-embedded banking built with Koxa for NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Workday and Dynamics 365 Business Central. Public user guide (Rev. 04/26) documents information reporting: real-time balances, posted transactions, on-demand refresh and native bank reconciliation. In-ERP Real-Time Payments and approvals were announced for the Oct 2025 pilot (IR release) but are not described in the public guide.' Keep rail RTP with notes 'announced (pilot)'. Set dual_approval_smb to 'unknown'. Reword the strength to 'One View Connect ERP-embedded information reporting (public guide) with in-ERP RTP and approvals announced in the Oct 2025 pilot'.

verifications.claim: Contract evidence cites the Online and Mobile Banking Service Agreements effective 4/8/2026 (personal S907, business S906).
verifications.finding: Both agreements have newer versions effective 9/17/2026 (linked from truist.com search results). I read both in full with pdf.js in the browser. The key clauses the chapter relies on are unchanged: Instant Transfers over an instant payment network at bank discretion; the RTP Instant Payment Bill Pay/RFP clause; per-wire OTP; domestic-only personal online wires; 7-calendar-day check retention; 'REIMBURSEMENT IS AVAILABLE FOR ... CERTAIN QUALIFYING IMPOSTER SCAMS'; ACH 8 pm ET deadline; Dual Approval Feature. New in the business version: an 'Approver Admin' role and the explicit 'must be enabled by the Business Profile Owner'.
verifications.resolution: Add S952/S953 as current-version sources alongside S906/S907 on the TFC-J05, J08, J09, J10, J11, J14 steps that rely on them. In J10/J14 REVIEW_AUTHORIZE, read the Dual Approval wording as: Approver or Approver Admin, feature enabled by the Business Profile Owner. No substantive capability changes.

verifications.claim: Open question: whether Wealth/Premier consumers can originate international wires online (Xe says yes).
verifications.finding: This can be answered now. The 9/17/2026 personal agreement limits the Wire Service to domestic wires: 'a payment order may be sent to initiate domestic wire transfers from eligible personal Accounts'. The personal fee schedule (eff. 09/28/2026) lists only online Outgoing Domestic ($20) and Book Transfer ($12) fees, with no online international fee. The Xe claim (S018) is contradicted.
verifications.resolution: Resolve the open question: personal online/mobile Wire Service = domestic wires (plus book transfers) for Truist Wealth and Premier relationships. Consumer international wires are teammate-assisted only ($65). S018's claim is contradicted.

verifications.claim: zelle: true, evidence THIRD_PARTY [S031, S001].
verifications.finding: The bank's own Zelle page (S001) describes the live service and its navigation. Per the schema, the evidence level should be CONFIRMED_BANK.
verifications.resolution: rail_participation.zelle evidence CONFIRMED_BANK; sources [S001, S031].

verifications.claim: Small-business online international wires are USD only ('USD only online per 2022 doc').
verifications.finding: The only evidence is the 2022 SunTrust transition PDF ('international (US dollar) wire transfers'). The current business agreement (9/17/2026) reserves the bank's right to convert any wire to a local currency. The current fee schedule lists an online 'International Wire Transfer $35' with no currency restriction. Neither current source says whether the OLB form lets the user choose a foreign currency.
verifications.resolution: Keep the claim hedged as '(USD only per 2022 transition doc; current currency options unverified)'. A screenshot or help text of the current OLB international wire form showing a currency selector (or not) would settle it.

verifications.claim: Commercial payments run in 'Digital Treasury / Treasury Manager'; J17/J18 originate ACH and wires in Treasury Manager.
verifications.finding: The Treasury Resource Center 'Platforms' menu (read in the browser, Nov 6 2026) lists only Truist One View, Digital Treasury and Truist One View Connect. Treasury Manager (ex-SunView) no longer appears. The Treasury Manager evidence (S045) is a 2022 transition PDF. No retirement notice was found.
verifications.resolution: Keep J17/J18 but note 'Treasury Manager evidence dates from 2022; not listed among current Treasury Resource Center platforms (Nov 2026)'. A Truist notice of Treasury Manager retirement or migration, or a current Treasury Manager guide, would settle it.

verifications.claim: Recent-changes list covers 2025-2026 money-movement launches.
verifications.finding: In Aug 2025 Truist added electronic direct deposit switching (with Atomic) to its digital account opening. It is money-movement-adjacent (moving payroll inflows to Truist). Reported by Zacks/Yahoo Finance (Dec 2025): 19% of digital applicants who used it completed the switch.
verifications.resolution: Add a recent change: 'Aug 2025: electronic direct deposit switching (Atomic) embedded in digital account opening; 19% of digital applicants who used it completed a switch (Zacks, Dec 2025) [S954].'

verifications.claim: Commercial dual-rail instant payments (RTP $10M, FedNow $1M); FedNow limit $1M (other_flags.fednow_limit).
verifications.finding: The Federal Reserve raised the FedNow per-transaction network limit from $1M to $10M effective November 2025. U.S. Bank's own Instant Payments API v2 page (rendered in browser) states a $10M limit for both TCH RTP and FedNow. The commercial RTP/FedNow marketing page (modified 2026-06-05) still says FedNow $1M — a stale bank page, not the current limit.
verifications.resolution: RTP and FedNow: $10M per transaction (U.S. Bank Instant Payments API; FedNow network limit since Nov 2025). U.S. Bank's commercial marketing page still shows FedNow $1M (stale).

verifications.claim: The 2023 FedNow fact sheet cited $1M for FedNow (and RTP $10M).
verifications.finding: In July 2023 the RTP limit was $1M and FedNow launched with a $500K maximum; the fact sheet lists '$1 million' and '$500,000' under 'The transaction limit' (layout ambiguous). The researcher's reading (FedNow $1M / RTP $10M in 2023) does not match either the PDF or the 2023 network limits. RTP went to $10M in Feb 2025; FedNow to $1M mid-2025 and $10M Nov 2025.
verifications.resolution: July 2023 fact sheet lists $1M and $500K without network labels; these match the then-current RTP $1M / FedNow $500K limits. Current limits are $10M for both. Open question resolved.

verifications.claim: Chapter's consumer inventory and 2025–2026 changes do not mention Payment Switch.
verifications.finding: U.S. Bank launched Payment Switch on Oct 19 2026: customers move recurring bills and subscriptions to a U.S. Bank debit or credit card from the Bills & Subscriptions dashboard in the mobile app, powered by Atomic (which also powers automated direct-deposit set-up; part of the 'Easy Switch' solution). The chapter's Oct 2026 release-note item ('streamlined direct-deposit enrollment') is the same Atomic programme but Payment Switch itself is missing.
verifications.resolution: Add sub-product 'Payment Switch' under USB-P05 (rail OTHER; vendor Atomic) and a recent change dated Oct 19 2026.

verifications.claim: Bill pay for business vendor 'Not named (third-party AP platform embedded; vendor not disclosed)'.
verifications.finding: U.S. Bank's own Aug 29 2025 Business Wire release (S117, previously only summary_only) states that bill pay for business is powered by Fiserv's CashFlow Central, built with Melio.
verifications.resolution: network_or_vendor: 'Fiserv CashFlow Central (built with Melio)'.

verifications.claim: Payee Choice former name: 'Supplier Prefer Pay (2017 supplier-enrollment product, S068)'.
verifications.finding: The 2017 release announced two separate products: Disbursements via Zelle (B2C) and Supplier Prefer Pay, a B2B supplier-enablement service moving suppliers from checks to virtual card and ACH. Payee Choice is a B2C payee-choice disbursement platform (RTP, Zelle, push-to-card, ACH, prepaid, check). Nothing links the two names.
verifications.resolution: Remove from Payee Choice former_names; note Supplier Prefer Pay as a historic B2B AP product.

verifications.claim: Commercial money-movement inventory is complete (SinglePoint, instant payments, Payee Choice, Zelle disbursements, push-to-card, Pay Smart, international).
verifications.finding: The commercial Accounts payable hub also markets U.S. Bank AP Optimizer® (invoice-to-pay automation), virtual credit cards, U.S. Bank prepaid solutions (B2C disbursement), check processing, and virtual account management. Card-based B2B payables and prepaid disbursements are money-movement products the chapter does not inventory.
verifications.resolution: Record as coverage gap: add a coverage note listing AP Optimizer®, virtual credit cards and U.S. Bank prepaid disbursements (commercial, rail OTHER) without journey mapping.

verifications.claim: SMB inventory does not include U.S. Bank invoicing.
verifications.finding: The Nov 2 2026 'Tour of business online banking' (S917, already in sources) promotes U.S. Bank invoicing: send branded invoices and receive payments by card or bank account; Digital Explorer lists a dedicated 'U.S. Bank invoicing' demo (/content/275). It appears in data only as a recent-changes mention, not as a product.
verifications.resolution: Add to coverage_self_assessment.known_gaps_in_evidence and open questions: 'U.S. Bank invoicing (SMB, card/bank-account collection) exists (S917) – rails and flow not mapped.'

verifications.claim: '...no foreign-currency or remittance product exists for consumers.'
verifications.finding: Digital Explorer's Transfer and pay channel includes 'Order foreign currency with the mobile app' (consumer foreign-cash ordering). It is not a remittance, so the remittance half of the claim stands; the foreign-currency half is wrong.
verifications.resolution: 'Consumers cannot send international wires digitally (branch or phone only) and have no remittance/cross-border transfer product; the only consumer FX capability is ordering foreign cash in the mobile app (S005, S050, S956).'

verifications.claim: Digital wires visible only to customers with ≥6 months history and an 'eligible direct-deposit account'.
verifications.finding: KB0209664 requires a checking, savings or money market account (a deposit account), ≥6 months as a customer and a registered cellular device; no direct-deposit requirement is stated.
verifications.resolution: 'eligible checking, savings or money market account (registered cellular device ≥3 business days)'.

verifications.claim: Action: 'Check the box acknowledging the payment can't be cancelled...; review details; select Send'.
verifications.finding: The live demo order is: 'Review before sending.' screen > 'Send $X' > full-screen 'Keep your money safe.' warning with checkbox 'I understand that once my payment is sent, it can't be canceled.' > Continue. The checkbox comes after Send, not before. The patched system_behavior field says this correctly but the action text was not updated.
verifications.resolution: Action rewritten to reflect Review > Send $X > 'Keep your money safe.' checkbox > Continue.

verifications.claim: Step numbers are sequential within each journey.
verifications.finding: The gap-fill patch broke numbering: J01 REVIEW_AUTHORIZE is numbered 1,2,3 between INITIATE 6 and EXECUTE_TRACK 9; J07 REVIEW_AUTHORIZE is 1,2 between INITIATE 4 and EXECUTE_TRACK 6; J09 SET_UP is 1,2 after DISCOVER 1. This is a data-integrity defect that will mis-sort steps in the consolidated deck.
verifications.resolution: Renumber sequentially as specified in the correction patch.

verifications.target: USB-J01 exception 'Authorized push payment scam (imposter)'; USB-J01/EXCEPTION/15
verifications.claim: Scam victims call the Fraud Liaison Center (877-595-6256).
verifications.finding: U.S. Bank pages differ: the Zelle for business page and Zelle support page direct scam/dispute contacts to 800-USBANKS (872-2657); the digital-payments-scam education page names the Fraud Liaison Center. Both are valid entry points; the chapter names only one.
verifications.resolution: 'Call 800-USBANKS (Zelle pages) or the Fraud Liaison Center 877-595-6256 (scam guidance page); no in-app scam-claim path.'

verifications.claim: Smart Assistant initiates bill payments (rail BILL_PAY).
verifications.finding: The Smart Assistant page gives 'Pay the statement balance on my credit card', 'Send 200 bucks to Tony' and 'Transfer $100 from savings to checking'. It does not name bill pay or Zelle. Paying a U.S. Bank card is an internal payment, not third-party bill pay.
verifications.resolution: USB-P07 rails: INTERNAL_TRANSFER, ZELLE (INFERRED), OTHER; sub-product description: 'P2P send (Zelle INFERRED), internal transfers and U.S. Bank credit-card payments; third-party bill pay via assistant not documented'.

verifications.claim: Oct 27 2026 Google Play release includes mobile deposit 'now with increased limits'.
verifications.finding: The Oct 27 2026 'What's new' text lists only direct-deposit enrollment, home value in net worth and transaction search. 'Quickly deposit checks, now with increased limits.' is in the undated 'About this app' description.
verifications.resolution: Reword as in the challenge.

verifications.claim: Standard outbound external transfer available in 1–3 business days.
verifications.finding: Bank pages conflict: the Transfer money page and KB0070109 say 1–3 business days, while KB0250043 says outbound funds are typically available two to three business days after initiation.
verifications.resolution: Keep '1–3 business days (KB0250043 says 2–3)'; add an open question.

verifications.claim: zelle = true, evidence THIRD_PARTY.
verifications.finding: U.S. Bank's own Zelle landing page confirms the service in its app and online banking, so the evidence level should be CONFIRMED_BANK (the zelle.com list corroborates).
verifications.resolution: zelle: true, CONFIRMED_BANK, [S002, S071].

verifications.target: rail_participation.fednow_send / push_to_card vs the participation baseline participation
verifications.claim: fednow_send = true and push_to_card = true (CONFIRMED_BANK).
verifications.finding: Challenge raised because the participation baseline → participation['us-bank'] shows fednow_send 'unknown' and push_to_card 'unknown'. Re-check: U.S. Bank's Instant Payments API lets clients send credit transfers via FedNow, and the Push to Card API sends to Visa/Mastercard debit cards. The bank chapter is right and the cross-bank matrix is stale.
verifications.resolution: No the research dataset change. Recommend the participation baseline fednow_send=true, push_to_card=true (commercial).

verifications.claim: International wire digital for business accounts only; consumers branch/phone; business digital fee $45 ($35 with Enhanced Payments); same-day only 7:30–3 CT; USD only.
verifications.finding: Tested whether consumers can now send international wires digitally (the July 2026 Enhanced Payments release made business international wires digital). KB0069815 still marks the digital route 'Business deposit accounts only'; the $45/$35 fees come from the Enhanced Payments comparison table; the cut-off and no-future-dating rules appear in the KB.
verifications.resolution: No change.

verifications.claim: Vantage/treasury-management capabilities are commercial-only; chapter has no SMB treasury-management product.
verifications.finding: Wells Fargo Business Banking markets 'Treasury Management Services' to small businesses, delivered through Wells Fargo Vantage and the Vantage app: wires (same-day or future-dated, approve/reject on smartphone), ACH payments (prepaid credit) for payroll/tax/vendor, Desktop Deposit (scanner RDC) and Vantage mobile deposit, ACH fraud filter pay/return decisions, dual custody, user transaction limits, ACH NOC/returns report. None of this is in the research dataset.
verifications.resolution: Add WF-P13-S08 'Treasury Management Services for Business Banking (via Vantage)' and add small_business to WF-P13.segments.

verifications.claim: Vantage is explicitly not for small business ('customers with personal and small business accounts... should download the Wells Fargo Mobile app'), so SMB gets no Tasks hub, Positive Pay decisions or payment-approval workflow.
verifications.finding: The App Store line steers personal/small-business account access to the consumer app, but the Business Banking site sells Treasury Management Services on Vantage to small businesses, including dual custody, wire approve/reject and ACH fraud-filter decisions. The conclusion that SMB gets no approval workflow is contradicted.
verifications.resolution: 'Small businesses use Wells Fargo Mobile/Business Online by default. Those that enroll in Treasury Management Services get Vantage, with dual custody, wire approve/reject and ACH fraud-filter decisions. The default SMB experience lacks a Tasks hub and approval workflow outside Direct Pay.'

verifications.claim: Small-business controls are uneven: Direct Pay has dual control, but Zelle, Business Bill Pay and Business Online wires can be executed by any single 'View and Transact' delegate.
verifications.finding: Supported for Business Online only, and as an absence-of-evidence inference: the OAA defines 'View and Transact' delegates and waives two-signature requirements, but no page states that dual approval is unavailable. SMBs on Vantage Treasury Management get dual custody for wires/ACH. Related step claims (WF-J17/REVIEW_AUTHORIZE/1, WF-J18/REVIEW_AUTHORIZE/1, WF-J03/REVIEW_AUTHORIZE/1) are tagged CONFIRMED_BANK.
verifications.resolution: 'Within Business Online, only Direct Pay documents dual control. Zelle, Business Bill Pay and wires can be executed by a single View and Transact delegate (INFERRED from OAA). SMBs on Vantage TM can require dual custody.' The related step-level 'no dual approval' assertions become INFERRED.

verifications.claim: Product inventory lists no official-check products.
verifications.finding: The online-services fee schedule lists Cashier's Checks orderable online (up to $2,000, delivered by mail, $10 + $8 delivery, $6,000 monthly limit) and Money Orders at branches ($5, up to $1,000), and online Stop Payment of checks/pre-authorized ACH ($30).
verifications.resolution: Add WF-P07-S03 'Cashier's checks (online order, up to $2,000, mailed) and money orders (branch, up to $1,000)', plus the online stop-payment MANAGE capability.

verifications.claim: Small-business payroll is covered only via Direct Pay.
verifications.finding: Business Online 'Transfer & Pay' lists 'Payroll solutions' (RUN Powered by ADP, third party) and Merchant Services (card acceptance with next-business-day funding) alongside Wires, Bill Pay, Direct Pay and Zelle. These are partner products, but the bank surfaces them in its money-movement menu.
verifications.resolution: Note in WF-P08.extra: Business Online Transfer & Pay also surfaces RUN Powered by ADP payroll (third party) and Merchant Services. Not modeled as WF products.

verifications.claim: Wallets listed: Paze, PayPal, Apple/Google/Samsung Pay.
verifications.finding: The bank also lists Garmin Pay among available digital wallets.
verifications.resolution: Add Garmin Pay to the WF-P11 wallet list.

verifications.claim: ExpressSend became available inside the Wells Fargo Mobile app (release notes 26.07.00, Jul 30, 2026).
verifications.finding: App Store version history first shows the ExpressSend note in 26.06.00 dated Jun 29, 2026. The dataset also keeps a later, corrected entry (obs:RC08), so the two conflict. research.md still says July 2026.
verifications.resolution: Remove obs:RC03. Keep the Jun 29, 2026 (v26.06.00) entry and the Sep 14, 2026 nationwide launch.

verifications.claim: Vantage mobile: domestic wire approvals (Apr/Jul 2025), Transfers create/edit/cancel (Jul 2025), Wires Status Search (Sep 2025), ACH Fraud Filter multi-item (Nov 2025), Tasks hub (Feb 2026).
verifications.finding: The iOS version history shows: Transfers experience 8.8.1 (Jul 1, 2025); ACH Fraud Filter multi-item 8.12.0 (Nov 12, 2025); Tasks hub 26.2.0 (Feb 17, 2026); domestic wire approvals 26.3.0 (Mar 17, 2026); Wires Status Search 26.9.0 (Sep 10, 2026). Two of the five dates are wrong. The Apr/Jul 2025 wire-approval dates could not be found on iOS.
verifications.resolution: Use the merged iOS timeline (WF-C009 resolution). Note that Android dates may differ.

verifications.claim: Vantage mobile 2026 (App Store dates)... supersedes the Apr 2025–Feb 2026 dating previously recorded.
verifications.finding: The gap-fill correction went too far. Several 2025 releases are real: mobile deposit PDF confirmations 8.8.0 (Jun 25, 2025), Transfers create/view/edit/cancel 8.8.1/8.8.2 (Jul 2025), credit-card accounts on home 8.11.0 (Oct 14, 2025), ACH Fraud Filter multi-item 8.12.0 (Nov 12, 2025). The 2026 items are correct.
verifications.resolution: Single entry: 'Vantage iOS: deposit PDF confirmations (Jun 2025); Transfers create/edit/cancel (Jul 2025); ACH Fraud Filter multi-item (Nov 2025); Tasks hub (Feb 2026); domestic wire approvals (Mar 2026); all wire approvals (Jul 2026); Positive Pay + Wires Status Search (Sep 2026); wire/tax/book/drawdown approvals + Cash Accounts (Oct 2026); home-screen payments tasks (Nov 2026).'

verifications.claim: Mobile approve/reject pending domestic wires (Apr/Jul 2025), tax payments, book transfers, drawdowns (Apr–Oct 2025 releases); 'Wires Status Search' (Sep 2025).
verifications.finding: These dates are a year early on iOS. Domestic wire approvals shipped Mar 17, 2026, all wire approvals Jul 21, 2026, and tax/book transfer/drawdown approvals Oct 13, 2026. Wires Status Search shipped Sep 10, 2026.
verifications.resolution: WF-P13-S02 / WF-J21: domestic wire approvals Mar 2026, all wire approvals Jul 2026, tax/book/drawdown approvals Oct 2026, Wires Status Search Sep 2026 (iOS App Store dates).

verifications.claim: Vantage (ex-CEO) mobile shipped payment approvals, Wires Status Search, ACH Fraud Filter multi-item decisions, a Tasks hub and RSA mobile token between Apr 2025 and Feb 2026 — fast cadence.
verifications.finding: Per the App Store history these shipped between Jul 2025 and Nov 2026. Payment approvals and Wires Status Search are 2026.
verifications.resolution: '...between Jul 2025 and Nov 2026 (monthly cadence)'

verifications.claim: Fargo is a differentiator: a gen-AI assistant that initiates Zelle payments (research.md: a capability no other top-4 bank markets).
verifications.finding: Bank of America markets the same capability for Erica. Wells Fargo's own pages call Fargo 'AI-powered' and do not say 'gen-AI'. What sets Fargo apart is its scale (more than 1B interactions; 3M Spanish-speaking users), not the capability itself.
verifications.resolution: 'Fargo (AI-powered assistant) can initiate Zelle sends and transfers. This is parity with peers (BofA Erica). WF differentiation is scale (>1B interactions; >3M Spanish-speaking users).'

verifications.claim: Only top-4 bank with a proprietary cross-border remittance product (ExpressSend) offering cash pickup in 12 countries.
verifications.finding: This rests on Wells Fargo's own claim ('the only major U.S. bank offering a dedicated mobile remittance service'). I found no independent peer check. Citi markets a proprietary 'Citi Global Transfer' service, so 'only proprietary cross-border product' is too broad. The cash-pickup uniqueness was not checked against peers.
verifications.resolution: Interim wording: 'Wells Fargo states it is "the only major U.S. bank offering a dedicated mobile remittance service"'. A peer check of Citi/JPM/BAC consumer remittance products (cash pickup, corridors) would settle it.

verifications.claim: capabilities.split = true
verifications.finding: 'Share costs, skip the awkwardness' is a marketing use case. No split-bill screen or multi-payer request is documented in the FAQ, the Addendum or the get-started steps. research.md itself says split is request-based.
verifications.resolution: split=false on WF-P01-S01/S02.

verifications.claim: states_shown: ['Accepted', 'Rejected']
verifications.finding: The public Instant Payments API reference gives the status vocabulary RECEIVED / PROCESSING / COMPLETED / REJECTED, with reason codes. The journey body uses this vocabulary, but the status_tracking block does not.
verifications.resolution: ['RECEIVED','PROCESSING','COMPLETED','REJECTED']

verifications.claim: ExpressSend states_shown: ['Sent', 'Available for pickup', 'Completed', 'Canceled'] (CONFIRMED_BANK)
verifications.finding: The mobile FAQ, mobile T&Cs, product page and press release mention only 'Activity' and real-time tracking. No status labels are published.
verifications.resolution: states_shown [] (labels unpublished), evidence INFERRED, where_visible 'Transfer Internationally > Activity'.

verifications.claim: Status vocabularies such as Processing/Sent, Paid, Pending approval, Approved, Processed, Invoiced, Open/Provisional credit are tagged CONFIRMED_BANK.
verifications.finding: Only Zelle (Completed/Pending/Scheduled), Digital Wires (7 statuses), transfers ('pending' after 8 pm PT), mobile deposit (processing/holds) and the Instant Payments API have published state labels. The other arrays are analyst reconstructions. J02 and J03 also copy 'Scheduled' and 'Failed' from J01, which do not apply to requests or receipts.
verifications.resolution: status_tracking.evidence = INFERRED for the listed journeys. J02/J03 states become [Pending, Completed].

verifications.claim: 'Insufficient funds => Transfer rejected' and 'Incoming payment returned => Sender notified' (CONFIRMED_BANK)
verifications.finding: Neither the Zelle FAQ nor the Addendum describes an NSF rejection or a return-to-sender notice. Addendum 10.G is a generic failure disclaimer, and the FAQ mentions email when a payment fails or is canceled.
verifications.resolution: Evidence INFERRED. The NSF path cites the FAQ failed-payment email.

verifications.claim: Bill Pay instant payments are sent over the RTP® network (The Clearing House).
verifications.finding: OAA §6(i) says the service 'may use' the RTP network 'or another third party network'. RTP is possible but not exclusive.
verifications.resolution: 'Instant payments sent via the RTP® network (or another third-party instant network per OAA §6(i))'. rail remains RTP.

verifications.claim: Bill Pay instant RfP payments are covered by the Bill Pay Payment Guarantee.
verifications.finding: The Guarantee page only carves instant RfP payments out of the deposit-account exclusion ('unless the transfer is an instant payment in response to a Request for Payment'). It also says instant payments cannot be stopped. There is no positive statement of coverage.
verifications.resolution: 'Not excluded from the Payment Guarantee (explicit RfP carve-out); no stop-payment protection'.

verifications.claim: RTP/FedNow credit posts in real time to Available Balance (CONFIRMED_BANK).
verifications.finding: The only bank evidence is the Early Pay Day exclusion footnote, which proves receipt, not posting behavior. Real-time posting is a network-rule inference.
verifications.resolution: WF-J15/EXECUTE_TRACK/1 evidence INFERRED.

verifications.claim: Network imposter-scam reimbursement policy (EWS, 2023) applies (CONFIRMED_BANK).
verifications.finding: Wells Fargo pages say only 'Qualifying imposters scams may be eligible for reimbursement'. They do not reference an Early Warning network policy.
verifications.resolution: Evidence THIRD_PARTY/INFERRED for the EWS link. The WF wording stays CONFIRMED_BANK.

verifications.claim: fees: 'None; stop payment $30'
verifications.finding: The $30 stop-payment fee in the online-services schedule applies to checks and pre-authorized ACH items. Bill Pay itself has no fee. Canceling a scheduled electronic Bill Pay payment carries no published fee.
verifications.resolution: 'Bill Pay: no fee; a $30 stop-payment fee may apply to stopping a mailed check.'

verifications.claim: Every published Digital Wires step references Wells Fargo Online, so the mobile wire flow is undocumented.
verifications.finding: The comparison chart lists Digital Wires enrollment as 'Online & mobile'. Mobile availability is therefore confirmed by the bank. Only the step-by-step mobile screens are unpublished.
verifications.resolution: 'Digital Wires is available online and in the app. Only web steps are published.'

verifications.claim: 'ExpressSend moved to mobile-only ... no branch/online path for new mobile enrollees' vs 'runs two parallel tracks'; research.md says app-only enrollment from July 2026.
verifications.finding: The bank says ExpressSend is 'moving' to mobile. The legacy branch/online FAQ is still live. Mobile T&C acceptance ends branch, web and phone access. ExpressSend Mobile itself is app-only. The two weaknesses should be merged, and the July date corrected (see WF-C007).
verifications.resolution: Use the merged wording in the WF-C025 proposed_correction.

verifications.claim: Recurring wires referenced in OAA §8(i).
verifications.finding: The provision is §8(h), 'Recurring and Future-Dated Orders'. §8(i) is Cancellation and Amendment.
verifications.resolution: notes: 'Recurring/future-dated wires (Preauthorized Orders) per OAA §8(h).'

verifications.claim: FedNow send participation could not be verified against the Federal Reserve participant list (XLSX unreachable).
verifications.finding: I parsed the live Fed XLSX (as of Nov 2, 2026). It lists 'WELLS FARGO BANK, NA, MINNEAPOLIS, MN'. The list has no send/receive flags (the RTN list is behind terms of use, which I did not accept). Combined with the bank's API routing to FEDNOW, fednow_send=true stands. Participation is now verified on the Fed list. the participation baseline participation (fednow_send 'unknown', push_to_card 'unknown') is stale relative to the research dataset.
verifications.resolution: Open question resolved. fednow_send=true with sources S912, S916, S952. Flag the participation baseline.

verifications.claim: sub_products_found: 37; research.md: 77 sources; research.md rail line: Push-to-card ✘ (no product found).
verifications.finding: the research dataset actually holds 40 sub-products and 112 sources, and rail_participation.push_to_card is true (Push to Card API, confirmed live). The research.md narrative is stale.
verifications.resolution: sub_products_found=42 after patch; research.md push-to-card ✔ (commercial).

verifications.claim: No evidence of dynamic scam interstitials or payment-purpose questions in the Zelle flow.
verifications.finding: A Jan 2026 press piece quotes Wells Fargo as saying it alerts customers to double-check the recipient. It is unclear whether that is an in-flow dynamic alert or static copy. Public bank pages show only static copy, recipient-name display and a first-time-recipient code.
verifications.resolution: Keep the weakness, qualified as 'not documented publicly'. An authenticated in-app Zelle send to a new recipient, or a WF statement describing the alert, would settle it.

verifications.claim: Access code text comes from short codes 93557/93733.
verifications.finding: Suspected error: the Zelle FAQ says Zelle texts come from 93557 or 93729.
verifications.resolution: Original claim stands: access codes come from 93557/93733. Zelle notifications come from 93557/93729 (already in CONFIRM_COMPLETE/1).

verifications.claim: Direct Pay is desktop-browser only (mobile not supported).
verifications.finding: Neither the current Direct Pay page nor the FAQ mentions a desktop restriction.
verifications.resolution: Original claim stands (CONFIRMED_BANK, S039).

verifications.claim: The first $400 of mobile deposits is generally available the same day.
verifications.finding: The Mobile Deposit FAQ gives only next-day availability for deposits before 9 pm PT and does not mention $400.
verifications.resolution: Original claim stands (CONFIRMED_BANK, S040).
